text: Love your family. Work superhard. Live your passion.
context: The three rules he says are the whole secret, ahead of any platform or tool.

text: I measure my success by how happy I am, not how big the business is or how much money I've made.
context: Why the Internet is absent from his three rules even though it built the brand.

text: You may not have connections, or an education, or wealth, but with enough passion and sweat, you can make anything happen.
context: His contrast between the ad budget that grew the wine shop and the sweat that grew the personal brand.

text: Content is king, but context is God.
context: The line he returns to: great content still fails if it ignores the platform it lands on.

text: There is no sale without the story; no knockout without the setup.
context: Jabs give value. The right hook, the ask, has no power without them.

text: Jabs are the lightweight pieces of content that benefit your customers by making them laugh, snicker, feel appreciated, or escape.
context: His definition of the jab. Right hooks are the calls to action that benefit the business.

text: On Facebook, the definition of great content is not the content that makes the most sales, but the content that people most want to share with others.
context: Platform context: shareability, not the direct sale, is what 'great' meant on Facebook.

text: There's a lot of talking and selling on Twitter, but not enough engagement, and that's a travesty, because Twitter is the cocktail party of the Internet — a place where listening well has tremendous benefits.
context: His complaint that brands treat a listening medium as a billboard.

text: Your story isn't powerful enough if all it does is lead the horse to water; it has to inspire the horse to drink, too.
context: Attention is not the same as action. The story has to move the person who heard it.

text: We're living in what I like to call the Thank You Economy, because only the companies that can figure out how to mind their manners in a very old-fashioned way — and do it authentically — are going to have a prayer of competing.
context: The book's thesis: social media made every market a small town again, and manners are the advantage.

text: Social media has transformed our world into one great big small town, dominated, as all vibrant towns used to be, by the strength of relationships, the currency of caring, and the power of word of mouth.
context: Why caring is not a soft extra. In a small town, word of mouth is the books.

text: Companies have to do their damndest to shape the word of mouth that circulates about them by treating each customer as though he or she were the most important customer in the world.
context: The small-town shopkeeper standard, applied at Internet scale.

text: Unless you are building a new company from the ground up and can install caring as your business's cornerstone, you have to be willing to embark on a cultural overhaul.
context: Caring has to be how the company is built, or the culture has to be rebuilt until every employee can mean it.
